sources.title: Adding Files to your Zotero Library
sources.version_or_commit: Living Zotero support page; page says last updated 2025-09-11; no app release selector.
sources.locator: Sections “Stored Files and Linked Files” and “Adding linked files,” rendered lines 72-103; “Accessing Files,” lines 105-109.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official Zotero support page and read its linked-versus-stored behavior and attach controls.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Stored files are the default and are copied into Zotero storage; linked files keep a link to the original, are not synced or deleted with the library item, and can use a linked attachment base directory for per-computer path differences.
sources.applicability: Useful product precedent for explicit copy versus link semantics, portability trade-offs, and UI wording. Its sync/group-library constraints are Zotero-specific.

sources.title: Why can’t Zotero find a linked file?
sources.version_or_commit: Living Zotero support page; last updated 2019-10-18.
sources.locator: “Why can’t Zotero find a linked file?” numbered causes and recovery, rendered lines 54-62.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official missing-linked-file guidance and read its failure cases and Locate guidance.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The documented causes include external move/delete, incorrectly configured base directory, and a linked file not synced by Zotero; the suggested path recovery is to find it and use Locate.
sources.applicability: Evidence for distinct missing, configuration, and transfer causes; supports explicit relink. Page is older and does not specify current implementation internals.

sources.title: Zotero attachment implementation: attachments.js
sources.version_or_commit: Upstream zotero/zotero main HEAD observed by read-only git ls-remote as commit 44fe83d98bcf9b982b74782dcc5f824c8ab9cb43 at 2026-10-12T01:08:50Z; no release tag asserted.
sources.locator: LINK_MODE_* and BASE_PATH_PLACEHOLDER around lines 2232-2245; importFromFile around 2278-2422; linkFromFile around 2491-2545; linkFromFileWithRelativePath around 2566-2636.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the exact commit-pinned source and inspected mode constants, distinct import/link entry points, and relative-path processing. No code was executed.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The code distinguishes imported from linked attachment modes. Relative linked paths are prefixed with attachments: and resolved against a configured base directory; indexing is conditional on the base directory and file being present.
sources.applicability: Concrete implementation example for keeping copy/import and reference/link operations distinct and making root-relative paths explicit. It is Zotero's implementation, not a standard.

sources.title: Automatically relocate linked files within current base directory (#2084)
sources.version_or_commit: Issue opened 2021-06-11; closed as completed 2022-10-08; GitHub page reports no linked branch or pull request.
sources.locator: Description and proposed search at rendered lines 151-163; status/activity at lines 184-226.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the upstream issue and read its problem statement, proposed filename/ancestor search, user confirmation, and closure activity.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The proposal applies when an absolute linked path fails and the user has a linked attachment base directory; proposed search begins with filename then successive parent folders and offers single/all repairs after showing candidate count.
sources.applicability: Real product history supporting bounded root search and confirmation. Closure is not itself proof of the exact shipped implementation; current source/UI is separate evidence.

sources.title: Zotero 7.0 Version History
sources.version_or_commit: Version-specific release entries 7.0.8 (2024-10-18) and 7.0.16 (2025-06-21); changelog page itself is living.
sources.locator: 7.0.8 bug-fix list at rendered lines 511-520; 7.0.16 fixes at lines 314-321.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official project changelog and used exact-text search to locate two attachment-path history entries.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: 7.0.8 records a fix for a potential auto-relink error; 7.0.16 records ignoring an invalid relative path while changing the linked attachment base directory.
sources.applicability: Shows the edge cases that required release fixes. Release notes describe fixes, not the underlying root cause or a guarantee against recurrence.

sources.title: Zotero linked-attachment user messages in upstream source
sources.version_or_commit: Same upstream commit 44fe83d98bcf9b982b74782dcc5f824c8ab9cb43 as S03; no release tag asserted.
sources.locator: File-not-found, auto-relink and manual-locate strings at lines 2865-2893.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the commit-pinned English locale source and inspected the missing and auto-relink messages.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The message describes an exact-path miss plus a same-name file under the configured base directory, then offers Relink, Relink All, and Locate Manually.
sources.applicability: UI-source evidence for candidate review and explicit confirmation; strings alone do not establish all search or matching logic.

sources.title: Relink clips to media files in Final Cut Pro for Mac
sources.version_or_commit: Apple Final Cut Pro for Mac user-guide page with URL token ver26f5c8c9; page does not state an app release number.
sources.locator: Relink clips procedure, rendered lines 645-699; filename matching, attribute analysis and explicit Relink Files action at lines 677-699.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official user-guide procedure for missing/renamed externally linked media.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The user chooses a file/folder; preliminary candidates use filenames and directory proximity; the app analyzes further attributes, lets the user remove bad matches, and commits only when Relink Files is selected. The command is not undoable.
sources.applicability: Cross-platform attachment analogy for reviewed, evidence-bearing relink. Media-specific frame-rate/channel criteria should not be copied wholesale.

sources.title: NSURL bookmarks and security-scoped file access
sources.version_or_commit: Current Apple Developer documentation page; bookmark API notes security-scoped bookmarks unavailable before macOS 10.7.3; no current SDK version selector.
sources.locator: Sections Bookmarks and Security Scope, Security-Scoped URLs, and Working with Bookmark Data; Apple page search/open content.
sources.observed_operation: Read the official Foundation URL bookmark documentation.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A bookmark usually survives move/rename/relaunch/restart. Sandboxed apps use security-scoped bookmarks for persistent user-granted access; resolved scoped URLs require balanced start/stop access calls. Usually is not an unconditional guarantee.
sources.applicability: A strong macOS-specific relocation/access adapter; not a portable project-wide file identifier.

sources.title: URLResourceKey.fileResourceIdentifierKey
sources.version_or_commit: Current Apple Developer Foundation API documentation; no OS release selector.
sources.locator: Discussion for fileResourceIdentifierKey and related file resource keys.
sources.observed_operation: Read the official Foundation API reference via indexed documentation content.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The resource identifier can compare resources, including same path or paths to the same inode on a filesystem, but the value is not persistent across system restarts.
sources.applicability: Evidence against treating this specific Apple resource ID as a durable cross-session key; platform details must be verified for supported OS/filesystem versions.

sources.title: FILE_ID_INFO (winbase.h)
sources.version_or_commit: Microsoft Learn page last updated 2024-02-22; requirements table lists Windows Server 2012 (desktop apps only).
sources.locator: Structure members and uniqueness semantics, rendered lines 24-49.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: FILE_ID_INFO combines a volume serial number with a 128-bit file ID; Microsoft says the pair identifies a file on one computer and can compare two open handles.
sources.applicability: Windows-local identity hint for comparing currently accessible candidates; not a cross-machine identity or a path.

sources.title: BY_HANDLE_FILE_INFORMATION (fileapi.h)
sources.version_or_commit: Microsoft Learn page last updated 2021-04-02; supported client Windows XP desktop apps and server Windows Server 2003 per page.
sources.locator: File ID remarks, filesystem caveats, and time precision, rendered lines 79-93.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official structure reference and read filesystem-specific ID behavior.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: IDs are filesystem-specific, may be reused or change; FAT IDs can change during rename/defragmentation; NTFS keeps an ID until deletion; timestamps differ in availability and precision by filesystem.
sources.applicability: Strong evidence that IDs and timestamps need a source-filesystem field and cannot be treated as universal durable identity.

sources.title: inode(7) Linux manual page
sources.version_or_commit: Linux man-pages 6.19 dated 2026-02-08 in indexed page content.
sources.locator: Description entries for stat.st_dev and stat.st_ino; online man page.
sources.observed_operation: Queried and read indexed man-pages content; direct browser open timed out, so the retained evidence is the returned primary-manual page content.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Inode numbers are unique only within one filesystem; device major/minor identify the hosting device for the stat result.
sources.applicability: Linux identity hints must include filesystem/device context and remain advisory across copies, mounts, and filesystems.

sources.title: open_by_handle_at(2) Linux manual page
sources.version_or_commit: Current online Linux man-pages entry; page reports Linux history from 2.6.39 / glibc 2.14.
sources.locator: name_to_handle_at() and open_by_handle_at() descriptions, NOTES, and VERSIONS.
sources.observed_operation: Read the primary man-page search result describing file-handle support and access conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Some filesystems do not support handle translation/open; handles can become stale; reopening by handle requires CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH.
sources.applicability: A stronger Linux mechanism cannot be a baseline requirement under the brief's no-elevation constraint.

sources.title: RFC 8089: The file URI Scheme
sources.locator: File-system name encoding at RFC pp. 4-5; local and non-local URI forms and Windows drive/UNC cases at pp. 16-18; rendered lines 303-347 and 713-722, 965-1005.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the RFC Editor text and read the normative syntax and path-encoding discussion.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The URI scheme represents local and non-local locations, with POSIX/Windows variants and encoding concerns; treating non-local URIs as local can be unsafe.
sources.applicability: Useful interop syntax evidence only. A file URI does not assert that the target exists, is accessible, or has the same identity.

sources.title: SQLite Transaction
sources.version_or_commit: Current SQLite documentation; no specific library build version selected.
sources.locator: Transactions, especially implicit and explicit transaction behavior, rendered lines 30-37.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Database reads and writes occur within transactions; commands start implicit transactions when none is active.
sources.applicability: A transaction is an implementation option for atomic record edits; it does not define the notebook's project-store format.

sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
sources.version_or_commit: Current SQLite documentation; WAL is documented as available beginning in SQLite 3.7.0 (2010-07-21).
sources.locator: Overview/concurrency at rendered lines 61-72 and 97-99; network/same-host restriction at lines 72 and 97.
sources.observed_operation: Opened SQLite WAL documentation and searched for writer, same-host, and network-filesystem constraints.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Readers and a writer can proceed concurrently, only one writer may append at a time, all processes must share one host, and WAL does not work over a network filesystem.
sources.applicability: For two windows on one local host, WAL may support readers alongside a writer; a record revision check is still needed for stale windows. Do not assume it works for projects on network storage.

sources.title: Naming Files, Paths, and Namespaces
sources.version_or_commit: Current Microsoft Learn Win32 documentation; no single Windows release selector.
sources.locator: Path forms, volume designators, case rules, character/path constraints, rendered lines 37-65 and 99-112.
sources.observed_operation: Opened Microsoft Learn file naming reference.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Windows supports drive-letter and UNC paths; volume letters are case-insensitive; filesystem component rules differ; default case assumptions should be avoided and NTFS can support case sensitivity.
sources.applicability: Path parsing/serialization and candidate comparison must be platform/filesystem aware.

sources.title: Apple File System FAQ
sources.version_or_commit: Apple APFS archived guide; page is an older guide, not a current OS-version guarantee.
sources.observed_operation: Read indexed Apple archive documentation for APFS volume variants.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: APFS has case-sensitive and case-insensitive macOS variants; case-insensitive is the usual default on macOS.
sources.applicability: Illustrates that even one OS can have different path-comparison semantics; confirm current target matrix before implementation.
